library(nlmixr2lib)

library(dplyr)

library(ggplot2)

# Model and source

```{r model-meta, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
mod <- readModelDb("Bukkems_2022_doravirine_placentaperfusion")
ui <- rxode2::rxode(mod)
cat("* Citation: ", ui$reference, "\n", sep = "")
cat("* Description: ", ui$description, "\n", sep = "")
```

* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s40262-022-01127-0>
* Open-access full text: <https://europepmc.org/article/MED/PMC9349081>

# What this file is, and what it is not

Bukkems and colleagues built two kinds of model:

| # | Model | Implementation | In this file? |
|---|-------|----------------|---------------|
| 1 | **Ex vivo cotyledon perfusion model** (Section 2.2, Figure 1A, Equations 1-7, Tables 1-2) | NONMEM 7.4 | **yes** |
| 2 | Whole-body maternal-fetal pregnancy PBPK model with a permeability-limited placenta (ESM Online Resource 10) | Simcyp V20 | no |

Model 2 is a Simcyp platform model: its organ volumes and blood flows,
tissue partition coefficients and CYP3A4 reference concentrations are computed
inside the Simcyp pregnancy population database and are not printed in the
paper, so it cannot be reconstructed from the publication. What transfers
between the two is a pair of numbers: the fitted maternal- and fetal-facing
transfer clearances, `CLpdm` and `CLpdf`, which the authors converted to
0.0507 and 0.0075 L/h/mL placenta and imputed into the placenta sub-model of
the Simcyp model (Section 3.3).

Model 1 is self-contained. It is five ODEs whose rate laws are printed as
Equations 1-7, whose volumes, flows and fractions unbound are in Table 1, and
whose two fitted clearances and the residual error are in Table 2. The
diffusion-only structure (Figure 1A) was selected over the diffusion +
P-glycoprotein structure (Figure 1B) because adding active transport did not
improve the fit (dOFV 0.007) and the transport clearance was tiny and
imprecise (Section 3.2).

# Population

The model describes an isolated human term placenta, not a patient
population. One intact cotyledon per placenta was perfused in a recirculating
(closed-closed) dual circuit, with maternal and fetal circulations both
closed. Doravirine was added to the maternal circulation in four experiments
(maternal-to-fetal direction) and to the fetal circulation in four
(fetal-to-maternal direction), at a nominal 0.96 mg/L to mimic the Cmax in
nonpregnant adults. Maternal and fetal flows were 12 and 6 mL/min, each
reservoir 200 mL, and samples were drawn over 180 min. The eight placentas
were from deliveries at 37-40 weeks (seven by caesarean section) with
cotyledon weights 18.9-64.4 g (ESM Online Resource 4).

# Source trace

| Quantity | Value | Source |
|----------|-------|--------|
| Maternal flow `Q_M` (`q_mat`) | 12 mL/min | Table 1 |
| Fetal flow `Q_F` (`q_fet`) | 6 mL/min | Table 1 |
| Maternal reservoir `V_MR` (`v_mres`) | 200 mL | Table 1 |
| Fetal reservoir `V_FR` (`v_fres`) | 200 mL | Table 1 |
| Maternal placenta `V_MP` (`v_mp`) | 5.08 mL (11.55% of 44.02) | Table 1 |
| Placental barrier `V_PB` (`v_pb`) | 4.86 mL (11.05% of 44.02) | Table 1 |
| Fetal placenta `V_FP` (`v_fp`) | 3.63 mL (8.25% of 44.02) | Table 1 |
| Ex vivo fraction unbound `FU` (`fu`) | 0.529 | Table 1 |
| Barrier fraction unbound `FUp` (`fu_pb`) | 0.01 | Table 1 |
| `CLpdm` (`lcl_pdm`) | 37.2 mL/min (95% CI 19.8-73.7) | Table 2 |
| `CLpdf` (`lcl_pdf`) | 5.5 mL/min (95% CI 3.1-9.8) | Table 2 |
| IIV `CLpdm`, `CLpdf` | fixed 100% CV | Table 2 |
| Additive residual error | 0.000007 ug/mL | Table 2 |
| Proportional residual error | 7.5% (maternal dosing), 12.6% (fetal dosing) | Table 2 |
| Maternal reservoir balance | Equation 1 | Section 2.2 |
| Maternal placenta balance | Equation 2 | Section 2.2 |
| Placental barrier balance | Equation 4 | Section 2.2 |
| Fetal placenta balance | Equation 6 | Section 2.2 |
| Fetal reservoir balance | Equation 7 | Section 2.2 |
| Observed reservoir curves | Figure 3 | Results 3.1 |
| Reservoir concentrations at 180 min | see below | Results 3.1 |

The two P-gp equations (3 and 5) replace equations 2 and 4 in the rejected
transport model; this file uses the diffusion-only equations 1, 2, 4, 6, 7.

# Simulation

Each experiment is one bolus of doravirine into the dosed reservoir, followed
for 180 min. The typical cotyledon (42 g) is simulated in both directions with
the random effects set to zero (the fixed 100% CV between-placenta variability
is exercised separately below).

```{r simulate}
modT <- rxode2::zeroRe(ui)
tgrid <- c(0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 45, 60, 90, 120, 150, 180)

solve_dir <- function(dose_cmt, dose_ug) {
  ev <- rxode2::et(amt = dose_ug, cmt = dose_cmt)
  for (tt in tgrid) ev <- rxode2::et(ev, tt, cmt = "maternal_reservoir")
  d <- as.data.frame(ev)
  d$dvid <- ifelse(d$evid == 0L, 1L, NA_integer_)
  as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(modT, d))[, c("time", "Cmaternal", "Cfetal")]
}

# The observed curves start near 1.1 mg/L rather than the nominal 0.96; the
# model is linear, so dose to the observed starting concentration (220 ug in
# 200 mL) to compare the transfer shape directly.
mtf <- solve_dir("maternal_reservoir", 220)
ftm <- solve_dir("fetal_reservoir", 220)
head(mtf)
```

# Replicate published figures

Figure 3 shows the mean maternal- and fetal-reservoir doravirine curves for
each perfusion direction. The points were read off the figure by the
maintainers at the plotted time points (reading precision about 0.02 mg/L).

```{r fig3-digitised}
fig3 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~direction, ~time, ~maternal, ~fetal,
  "MTF",   0, 1.10, 0.00,
  "MTF",   5, 0.88, 0.01,
  "MTF",  10, 0.76, 0.02,
  "MTF",  15, 0.70, 0.04,
  "MTF",  20, 0.63, 0.05,
  "MTF",  25, 0.57, 0.07,
  "MTF",  30, 0.56, 0.08,
  "MTF",  45, 0.49, 0.12,
  "MTF",  60, 0.44, 0.16,
  "MTF",  90, 0.40, 0.20,
  "MTF", 120, 0.38, 0.23,
  "MTF", 150, 0.36, 0.26,
  "MTF", 180, 0.34, 0.28,
  "FTM",   0, 0.00, 1.10,
  "FTM",   5, 0.01, 1.00,
  "FTM",  10, 0.01, 1.00,
  "FTM",  15, 0.02, 0.95,
  "FTM",  20, 0.03, 0.92,
  "FTM",  25, 0.04, 0.90,
  "FTM",  30, 0.06, 0.88,
  "FTM",  45, 0.10, 0.83,
  "FTM",  60, 0.14, 0.75,
  "FTM",  90, 0.20, 0.64,
  "FTM", 120, 0.22, 0.57,
  "FTM", 150, 0.24, 0.50,
  "FTM", 180, 0.26, 0.45
)

sim_long <- bind_rows(
  mtf |> mutate(direction = "MTF"),
  ftm |> mutate(direction = "FTM")
) |>
  pivot_longer(c(Cmaternal, Cfetal), names_to = "reservoir", values_to = "sim") |>
  mutate(reservoir = recode(reservoir, Cmaternal = "maternal", Cfetal = "fetal"))

obs_long <- fig3 |>
  pivot_longer(c(maternal, fetal), names_to = "reservoir", values_to = "obs")
```

```{r fig3-plot, fig.width = 7.5, fig.height = 4}
ggplot(sim_long, aes(time, sim, colour = reservoir)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(
    data = obs_long, aes(time, obs, colour = reservoir),
    inherit.aes = FALSE, shape = 1
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ factor(direction, c("MTF", "FTM")),
    labeller = as_labeller(c(MTF = "Maternal-to-fetal", FTM = "Fetal-to-maternal"))
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (min)", y = "Doravirine (mg/L)", colour = "Reservoir",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 3 of Bukkems 2022. Lines: this model (42 g cotyledon); circles: the paper's means read off the figure."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

The transfer shape is reproduced in both directions. The model is for the
typical 42 g cotyledon, whereas the observed curves are means over placentas
of 18.9-64.4 g (median 32.55 g); a smaller-than-typical cotyledon transfers
slightly less, which is why the dosed reservoir in the model sits a little
below the observed mean late in the fetal-to-maternal experiment.

```{r fig3-gates}
cmp <- sim_long |>
  inner_join(obs_long, by = c("direction", "time", "reservoir")) |>
  filter(time > 0)
cmp_dosed <- cmp |>
  filter((direction == "MTF" & reservoir == "maternal") |
    (direction == "FTM" & reservoir == "fetal"))
stopifnot(
  # Dosed-reservoir decline: a wrong flow, volume or clearance moves the
  # whole curve by tens of percent.
  median(abs(cmp_dosed$sim - cmp_dosed$obs) / cmp_dosed$obs) < 0.12,
  # Whole-figure envelope, both reservoirs, both directions.
  quantile(abs(cmp$sim - cmp$obs), 0.9) < 0.1
)
```

# Transfer ratios reported in the text

The reservoir concentrations at 180 min are reported in Results 3.1.
Because the model is linear in dose, the fetal:maternal reservoir ratios at
the end of the experiment are independent of the starting concentration, so
they are a clean check on the transfer clearances alone.

```{r ratios}
end_mtf <- mtf[mtf$time == 180, ]
end_ftm <- ftm[ftm$time == 180, ]
ratios <- tibble::tibble(
  Direction = c("Maternal-to-fetal", "Fetal-to-maternal"),
  `Ratio (into:out of)` = c("fetal:maternal", "maternal:fetal"),
  `Reported (Results 3.1)` = c(0.28 / 0.34, 0.28 / 0.42),
  `Model` = c(
    end_mtf$Cfetal / end_mtf$Cmaternal,
    end_ftm$Cmaternal / end_ftm$Cfetal
  )
)
knitr::kable(ratios, digits = 3)

stopifnot(
  # Maternal-to-fetal transfer ratio at 180 min: text 0.82, model within 10%.
  abs(ratios$Model[1] - 0.28 / 0.34) < 0.10,
  # Fetal-to-maternal transfer ratio at 180 min: text ~0.67, model within 15%.
  abs(ratios$Model[2] - 0.28 / 0.42) < 0.15
)
```

The maternal-to-fetal ratio of `r round(ratios$Model[1], 2)` matches the
reported 0.82; doravirine crosses the placenta almost completely over the
experiment, consistent with the paper's conclusion that it is a
blood-flow-limited, extensively transferred compound.

# Between-placenta variability

The fit carried a between-placenta variability fixed at 100% CV on both
transfer clearances (Table 2). Simulating a cohort of 200 cotyledons in the
maternal-to-fetal direction shows the spread this produces in the fetal
reservoir at 180 min.

```{r vpc}
set.seed(74)
n_cot <- 200
ev <- rxode2::et(amt = 220, cmt = "maternal_reservoir")
for (tt in c(60, 120, 180)) ev <- rxode2::et(ev, tt, cmt = "maternal_reservoir")
d <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(n_cot), function(i) {
  x <- as.data.frame(ev)
  x$id <- i
  x
}))
d$dvid <- ifelse(d$evid == 0L, 1L, NA_integer_)
sim_pop <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(ui, d))
f180 <- sim_pop$Cfetal[sim_pop$time == 180]
summary(f180)
stopifnot(
  # The typical-value fetal reservoir at 180 min (~0.26) sits inside the
  # cohort, and the 100% CV spread is wide.
  median(f180) > 0.15, median(f180) < 0.40,
  stats::IQR(f180) > 0.02
)
```

# NCA

The paper reports no non-compartmental parameters for the ex vivo experiment,
so there is no published NCA to compare with. For reference, PKNCA summarises
the simulated dosed- and receiving-reservoir exposures over the 180-min
maternal-to-fetal experiment.

```{r pknca}
conc <- mtf |>
  pivot_longer(c(Cmaternal, Cfetal), names_to = "reservoir", values_to = "conc") |>
  mutate(id = 1L, reservoir = recode(reservoir, Cmaternal = "maternal", Cfetal = "fetal")) |>
  filter(!is.na(conc))
dose_df <- tibble::tibble(
  id = 1L, time = 0,
  amt = c(220, 0),
  reservoir = c("maternal", "fetal")
)
conc_obj <- PKNCAconc(conc, conc ~ time | reservoir + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | reservoir + id)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 180, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
nca <- pk.nca(PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
as.data.frame(nca$result) |>
  select(reservoir, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Reservoir" = reservoir,
    "Cmax (mg/L)" = cmax,
    "Tmax (min)" = tmax,
    "AUC0-180 (min*mg/L)" = auclast
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Only the ex vivo model is packaged.** The whole-body maternal-fetal
  pregnancy PBPK model is a Simcyp platform model whose physiological
  parameters are database outputs not printed in the paper, so it is out of
  scope. The two quantities that bridge the two models, `CLpdm` and `CLpdf`,
  are in this file.
* **Typical 42 g cotyledon.** Table 1 standardises the placental sub-volumes
  to a 42 g (44.02 mL) cotyledon and Table 2 reports `CLpdm` / `CLpdf` for
  that typical cotyledon (footnote a). The paper scaled volumes and clearances
  by each placenta's individual cotyledon weight when fitting; this packaged
  typical-value model fixes them at the 42 g reference, so the simulated
  curves track the typical rather than a weight-specific cotyledon.
* **Single proportional residual error.** Table 2 reports a proportional
  residual error of 7.5% CV after dosing in the maternal compartment and
  12.6% after dosing in the fetal compartment. The model carries one
  proportional residual (`propSd`), set to the maternal-dosing value
  (7.5% CV, back-transformed SD 0.0749); the fetal-dosing value
  (12.6% CV, SD 0.1255) is recorded here and in the model-file comment. The
  additive residual error (0.000007 ug/mL) is negligible.
* **Diffusion-only structure.** The P-glycoprotein transport model (Figure 1B,
  Equations 3 and 5) was rejected by the authors and is not implemented.
* **Observed starting concentration.** The simulation doses to the observed
  starting concentration of about 1.1 mg/L (220 ug in 200 mL) rather than the
  nominal 0.96 mg/L, so the linear model's transfer shape overlays the figure
  directly. The transfer ratios checked above are dose-independent.
* **Closed-open sensitivity analysis not packaged.** A sensitivity analysis
  re-fit the same structure to closed-open perfusions (dosed circulation
  recirculating, other single-pass) and estimated `CLpdm` 11.0 mL/min
  (95% CI 5.6-22.7) and `CLpdf` 4.3 mL/min (95% CI 2.3-8.3) (ESM Online
  Resource 19). These configuration-specific estimates are reported here for
  completeness; the closed-closed fit used for the primary PBPK predictions is
  the one packaged.
* **Figure 3 values were read off the figure** and carry about 0.02 mg/L of
  reading error; the observed means in that figure are not otherwise used.
